conflicts_resolved.topic: Use cases implementing inbound ports vs doing I/O
conflicts_resolved.a: A1C-005 — use cases should implement inbound ports
conflicts_resolved.b: A1P-001 — ExportGraphImageUseCase should not do DOM I/O
conflicts_resolved.decision: Both. Inbound port on the use case; I/O on an outbound adapter. Recorded on HEX-015.

conflicts_resolved.b: A5-007 remove empty frozen packages from bounded_contexts
conflicts_resolved.decision: Merge as HEX-025. transaction-system is frozen but implemented — do not delete. architectural-enforcement/code-generation are empty scaffolds.
GOD-010 depends_on HEX-005. Do not split the adapter until the port has a single owner.

killed.reason: Size-only / style-only modernization dropped by A4 (var→const, for→for-of, enum→union without correctness benefit).
PlaceOrderPort / RestControllerPort / CreativeProductionPort 'duplicates' are test fixtures or generated bundle mirrors — not dual ownership.

findings.title: Generated customer domain ports import infrastructure error types
findings.coupling: Outbound ports in generated src/domain bind Result's error channel to infrastructure FireflyError/LLMError. Type-only does not invert the dependency. Same pattern in 13+ Adobe/LLM templates.
findings.benefit: boundary integrity — customer domain compiles without adobe/llm adapter modules; vendor errors can change without rewriting ports
findings.recommendation: Move failure unions into domain (e.g. CreativeProductionError) and map adapter errors at the adapter. Repeat for every template port that imports ../../../infrastructure/.
findings.orchestrator_notes: Verified. The comment claiming 'deliberate decoupling' is inverted: domain still names an infrastructure type.

findings.title: GenerateProjectUseCase performs Node filesystem I/O instead of a driven port
findings.coupling: Application layer imports node:fs/promises and node:path while also injecting generator/exporter/materializer ports.
findings.benefit: testability — generation can be exercised without a real filesystem or /tmp side effects
findings.recommendation: Move mkdir/write/realpath/lstat/rm/readFile behind an owned outbound FileSystemPort. See ADR on whether this shares a kernel FS port with HEX-007.

findings.title: Manifest generate HTTP routes compose adapters, domain factories, and transaction infra
findings.coupling: Same new EnvironmentSecretVaultAdapter / LLMProviderSelectorAdapter / InMemoryTransactionManager pattern in generate/route.ts, local/route.ts, spec/route.ts, stage/route.ts — bypassing wire.server.ts.
findings.benefit: testability — routes become request mapping; LLM/tx providers swap at one composition root
findings.recommendation: Move adapter construction into wire.server.ts; route only parses HTTP and invokes a pre-wired inbound port.

findings.title: Application ports and mappers are typed on @hexagen/sync Manifest
findings.coupling: Application contracts cannot compile without the sync CLI package. Manifest schema is owned by project-configuration.
findings.benefit: boundary integrity — generation/wizard stay independent of the sync engine
findings.recommendation: Import Manifest from @hexagen/project-configuration (or a BC-owned DTO). Restrict @hexagen/sync to ExternalSyncEngineAdapter.

findings.title: ManifestGenerationPort is owned by two contexts with incompatible contracts
findings.coupling: Same type name, different methods (execute vs generateTopology/generateAdapters/generateManifestPipeline). No shared type identity.
findings.benefit: boundary integrity — one port, one owner; adapters cannot silently satisfy the wrong contract
findings.recommendation: Keep one owning context. mcp-server should import a distinctly named outbound contract (e.g. StagedManifestGenerationPort) or the published inbound port.
findings.orchestrator_notes: Command used: python3 scan of export (interface|type) \w*Port — 7 names in >1 file; this pair is a real contract clash, not a re-export.

findings.title: ProjectConfigurationReadPort is independently declared in three packages
findings.coupling: Three type identities for one capability. Consumers can implement the wrong copy.
findings.benefit: boundary integrity — single type identity; signature changes compile everywhere
findings.recommendation: Publish from project-configuration only; mcp-server and sync import that type.

findings.title: FileSystemPort is declared twice with disjoint APIs
findings.coupling: Homonymous ports are not substitutable. HEX-002 will need a write/mkdir port — must not silently reuse the wrong FileSystemPort.
findings.benefit: correctness — adapters cannot be wired to the wrong FS contract
findings.recommendation: Rename to ManifestMergeFsPort vs GeneratorFsPort (or extract a shared-kernel FsPort if operations truly belong together). ADR required.

findings.title: Two incompatible SecretVaultPort contracts in one package
findings.coupling: EnvironmentSecretVaultAdapter implements getSecret; SecureChatDispatchUseCase depends on retrieve(); package barrel can export the domain type.
findings.benefit: correctness — no silent type collision at the package export
findings.recommendation: Keep two named ports if both capabilities are needed (EnvSecretLookupPort vs EncryptedVaultPort). Do not share the name SecretVaultPort.

findings.coupling: test:jest can still execute a second, stale suite. Root jest.setup.js will throw if loaded under Vitest.
findings.benefit: testability — two runners on the same files can disagree
findings.recommendation: Remove test:jest, jest/ts-jest/jest-environment-jsdom, jest.config.cjs, jest.resolver.cjs, both jest.setup.js files, and the unused ui-projection-compiler Jest config.

findings.title: Published packages advertise Node >=20 while the repo/CI floor is >=22.7.0
findings.coupling: CI is Node 22.7 / 22.12 (ADR-0036 assumes Node 22). npm will not refuse Node 20 installs of hexagen/hexagen-lint.
findings.benefit: runtime — consumers on Node 20 are outside what this monorepo builds and tests
findings.recommendation: Align engines.node with root >=22.7.0, or document a tested 20.x matrix and run CI on 20. ADR required.

findings.title: @hexagen/security is Node16/ESM-with-.js while the monorepo floor is bundler

evidence.excerpt:

  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "Node16",
    "moduleResolution": "Node16",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "declaration": true,

findings.coupling: Does not extend tsconfig.base.json. main points at src/index.ts. No in-repo consumers yet.
findings.benefit: correctness — Node16 requires .js specifiers at emit time; bundler consumers resolve .ts source
findings.recommendation: Extend tsconfig.base.json (bundler), drop .js specifiers, point main/types at dist, add engines.node matching root.

findings.title: ai-pipeline tsconfig.test.json is CommonJS + @types/jest while the package is ESM Vitest
findings.coupling: Only commonjs/node test config in the repo. Tests import from vitest.
findings.benefit: correctness — CJS + jest types will mis-type import.meta and Vitest globals
findings.recommendation: Delete tsconfig.test.json or rewrite it to inherit ESM/bundler with types: ["node"] (or vitest/globals).

findings.title: catch-and-rethrow stringifies the original error and drops Error.cause
findings.coupling: Same repo already uses { cause } in idb-saved-projects.adapter.ts. Error.cause is in the ES2022 floor.
findings.benefit: correctness — stack, errno, and nested fetch failures are lost
findings.recommendation: throw new Error(msg, { cause: error }) at these rethrow sites. No lib raise.

findings.title: Retry helper wraps an already-thenable in new Promise and can hang if the inner call throws
findings.coupling: No reject path. A sync throw inside setTimeout is unhandled and the outer Promise stays pending.
findings.benefit: correctness — failures must propagate
findings.recommendation: await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay)); return createCloudConnectionUseCaseWithRetry(...)(...). Do not use Promise.withResolvers unless lib is raised to ES2024.
